newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA frees kidnapped Spaniard - police.
newsitem.headline: ETA frees kidnapped Spaniard - police.

text.p: The Basque guerrilla group ETA freed a kidnapped Basque businessman, Cosme Delclaux, early on Tuesday, police said.

Delclaux had been held captive for 232 days and Spanish media reported last month that his family had paid a ransom for his release. The Spanish government has said repeatedly the kidnappings of Delclaux and another man were a major obstacle to any peace talks with ETA.

Spanish state radio said Delclaux, 34, was found tied to a tree in the Basque country in the early hours of Tuesday after Basque police received an anonymous phone call informing of his release. He was brought to a police station in Durango in the Basque province of Vizcaya.
Delclaux was kidnapped on November 11, 1996 in the Basque country where businessmen have long complained that ETA runs a campaign of extortion aimed at them.

ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, still holds former prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, kidnapped almost two years ago. The Basque rebels have waged a 29-year struggle for independence from Spain in which 800 people have been killed.
Spain's centre-right government has insisted that no peace talks with ETA were possible as long as the group holds hostages.
